scope: World cinema released before 2000: Hollywood classics, European and Asian cinema, famous directors, actors, scenes, quotes, behind the scenes stories. Not Soviet films (soviet_film has them).

World cinema from 2000 on: blockbusters, franchises, animated features from big studios, festivals, Oscars, directors, behind the scenes stories. Not superhero comics lore (heroes) and not cartoons as such (cartoons).
Soviet and early Russian cinema: Gaidai, Ryazanov, Tarkovsky, Mosfilm and Lenfilm, famous comedies, quotes that became sayings, actors, filming stories. Live action only (cartoons has the animation).
World TV series of every era: Friends, Game of Thrones, Breaking Bad, The Simpsons as a show, Sherlock, anime series, Netflix hits, sitcoms; characters, actors, records, filming stories.
Soviet and Russian television: KVN, What? Where? When?, Field of Miracles, Good Night Little Ones, New Year broadcasts, famous presenters, TV series, Soviet TV oddities. No current politics.
Animation from everywhere and every era: Soyuzmultfilm (Nu Pogodi, Cheburashka, Prostokvashino), Disney, Pixar, DreamWorks, Ghibli, Tom and Jerry, anime films; voices, characters, how they were made.
Comic books and superheroes: Marvel, DC, their films and origins, villains, creators like Stan Lee, European comics (Tintin, Asterix), manga, comic history.
Video games and consoles up to about 2005: arcades, Tetris, Super Mario, Sega, Dendy and the NES, PlayStation 1 and 2, PC classics like Doom, Heroes III, StarCraft, Counter-Strike 1.6.

Video games from about 2005 on: Minecraft, GTA V, The Witcher, Dota 2, Fortnite, Among Us, The Last of Us, esports, consoles, mobile hits, records and development stories. Avoid facts that change month to month.
Board and card games and puzzles: chess, draughts, Monopoly, Scrabble, Go, playing cards, dice, Rubik's cube, crosswords, sudoku, party games; origins, rules oddities and records.
World popular music before 2000: the Beatles, Queen, ABBA, Michael Jackson, Elvis, Madonna, rock, disco, jazz greats, famous songs and albums, band stories. Not Russian or Soviet music (ru_music).

World popular music from 2000 on: pop, hip hop, K-pop, Eurovision, streaming records, festivals, famous songs, artists and their stories. Not Russian music (ru_music). Avoid facts that change month to month.
Soviet and Russian popular music of every era: estrada, VIA bands, Soviet rock (Kino, Aquarium, DDT), Pugacheva, the 90s and 2000s pop, Russian hip hop, film songs, famous lyrics. No politics.
Classical music, opera and ballet: composers (Mozart, Beethoven, Tchaikovsky, Bach, Vivaldi), famous works, instruments, orchestras, the Bolshoi, odd composer stories.
Painting and sculpture: the Mona Lisa, Van Gogh, Picasso, Dali, Michelangelo, Russian painters (Repin, Shishkin, Aivazovsky, Malevich), museums, thefts and forgeries, how famous works were made.
Famous buildings and landmarks: the wonders of the world, the Eiffel Tower, pyramids, the Kremlin, skyscrapers, bridges, castles, architects, how and why they were built.
Money and economics in everyday terms: the history of coins and banknotes, currencies of the world, banks, prices through history, famous fortunes, stock market oddities, inflation stories.
World brands and companies: where names and logos came from, what famous companies first made (Nokia, Nintendo, Samsung), famous products, slogans, ads, business blunders. Text only, no pictures.
Antiquity: Egypt, Mesopotamia, Greece, Rome, Persia, China, the Maya; pharaohs, emperors, everyday life, inventions, wonders and wars of the ancient world.
Myths of the world: Greek and Roman gods and heroes, Norse, Egyptian, Slavic folklore (Perun, Baba Yaga as a folk figure), Japanese and other myths, monsters, words that come from myths.
The Middle Ages worldwide, roughly 500 to 1500: knights, castles, Vikings, samurai, the Mongols, crusades, plague, medieval daily life, food, medicine, inventions and oddities.

World history of 1900 to 1999: inventions that changed life, the space race, famous events, revolutions, the fall of the Berlin Wall, everyday life in the century. Keep wars to well established facts, no gore.
The Soviet Union 1922 to 1991: everyday life, shortages and queues, Soviet brands and products, the space programme, the Olympics 80, holidays, pioneers, famous Soviet things and their stories.
The 1990s around the world and in Russia: Tamagotchi, pagers, Dendy, MTV, Titanic, the first websites, fashion, music, events, everyday life. No current politics.
Russian history up to 1917: Kievan Rus, Ivan the Terrible, Peter the Great, Catherine the Great, 1812, the tsars, explorers, reforms, everyday life, odd laws and stories.

Political history and trivia of Russia and the USSR up to about 2000 only: how the state worked, the Duma, constitutions, symbols, the flag and anthem, famous quotes, Soviet leaders as history. NOTHING about current leaders, current events, wars or elections after 2000.
Monarchs and rulers of the world through history: kings, queens, emperors, pharaohs, khans, their habits, titles, scandals, crowns and odd records. Not modern politicians.

Famous conspiracy theories: the Moon landing, flat Earth, Area 51, Paul is dead, reptilians, chemtrails, the Illuminati, Shakespeare authorship. Ask what a theory claims, where it came from, or what the evidence actually shows; the fact always gives the real answer. Never present a theory as true. kids false.

Famous mysteries, solved and unsolved: the Dyatlov Pass, the Voynich manuscript, the Mary Celeste, Stonehenge, the Bermuda Triangle, the Tunguska event, lost cities and treasures. The fact gives the best current explanation.

Famous heists, cons, forgeries and detective stories: the Mona Lisa theft, the selling of the Eiffel Tower, Ponzi, famous escapes, great detectives (Sherlock Holmes, Poirot) and real investigations. No gore. kids false.

Common misconceptions everyone believes: goldfish memory, the Great Wall seen from space, Napoleon's height, Vikings' horned helmets, the 10% of the brain. Ask what is really true; the fact busts the myth.
The human body: organs, bones, senses, sleep, blood, genes, records of the body, odd facts about how we work.
Medicine and its history: famous discoveries (penicillin, vaccines, anaesthesia), strange old treatments, doctors and scientists, how medicines got their names, hospitals, records.
Space and astronomy: planets, stars, the Moon, Gagarin and the space race, the ISS, telescopes, cosmonauts and astronauts, space records and oddities.
Everyday physics and chemistry: why the sky is blue, how a microwave works, why ice floats, the periodic table, light, sound, electricity, famous experiments, explained simply.

Inventions and inventors from every era: everyday objects (the zip, the fork, the toilet), accidental inventions, who really invented what, patents and odd early versions. Not computers and phones (gadgets).
Computers, phones and electronics: the first computers, Apple, Microsoft, Nokia, the mouse, the floppy disk, the first SMS, the internet's infrastructure, how gadgets work, tech history.

Internet culture: famous memes and where they came from, emoji, viral videos, YouTube, Wikipedia, social networks, internet slang, the first website, records. International memes plus well known Runet ones. Nothing offensive.
The 2000s around the world and in Russia: flip phones, ICQ, MP3 players, the first iPhone, reality TV, music, films, fashion, everyday life. No current politics.
Animals with surprising abilities and habits, on land and in the air: mammals, birds, insects, reptiles; records, senses, odd behaviour. Not sea creatures (sea) or extinct ones (dinosaurs).
Oceans, seas and their creatures: whales, octopuses, sharks, deep sea life, coral reefs, tides, shipwrecks, the deepest places.
Dinosaurs and extinct animals: T. rex, mammoths, dodos, sabre tooth cats, how fossils are found, what we got wrong about dinosaurs, extinction events.
Our planet: volcanoes, earthquakes, weather, climate, records of heat and cold, rivers, mountains, deserts, rocks and minerals, natural disasters, natural wonders.
Plants, trees, flowers and mushrooms: record trees, carnivorous plants, poisons, vegetables and fruits that are not what you think, where crops came from, fungi oddities.
Geography oddities: borders, time zones, enclaves, islands, extreme places, odd place names, records of countries and cities. Not capitals and flags as such (countries).
Countries of the world: capitals, flags described in words, national symbols, languages spoken, populations, odd national laws and customs, how countries got their names.
Russia's geography and places: cities, rivers, Baikal, Kamchatka, the Trans-Siberian, regions, records, landmarks, how places got their names, nature reserves.

Languages and words: where words come from, alphabets, the most spoken languages, untranslatable words, loanwords between Russian and other languages, sayings, writing systems. Questions must work for a Russian speaker; English text may name Russian words in transliteration.
Holidays and traditions around the world: New Year, Christmas, Maslenitsa, Halloween, Chinese New Year, Diwali, odd local festivals, where customs come from, holiday food and gifts.
Food of the world: dishes and where they really come from, ingredients, spices, cooking science, famous chefs, food records, fast food history, Russian and Soviet food too.
Drinks of the world: coffee, tea, cocoa, lemonade and soda history, juices, mineral water, wine, beer and cocktails as culture and history (no encouraging drinking). kids false for alcohol questions.
Clothes and fashion: where jeans, the little black dress, sneakers and the tie came from, famous designers and brands, odd fashions in history, hair and make up history.
Transport: cars and car brands, trains, metros, planes, ships, bicycles, records of speed and size, the first ones, Soviet cars, how transport works.
Famous people from history, science, art and exploration: their habits, nicknames, surprising facts, who did what first, explorers and travellers. Not current politicians.
Football (soccer): World Cups, famous players and clubs, rules and their origins, records, Soviet and Russian football history, legendary matches. Avoid records that could change this season.
The Olympic Games ancient and modern, summer and winter: odd old sports, legendary athletes, mascots (Misha 1980), records, symbols and traditions.
Sports of the world other than football and the Olympics as such: tennis, hockey, chess as a sport, Formula 1, boxing, odd sports, rules and their origins, records that are settled history.

Classic literature of the world and Russia before about 1950: Pushkin, Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Gogol, Chekhov, Bulgakov, Shakespeare, Dickens, Dumas, Verne, Conan Doyle; characters, plots, author stories.

Books from about 1950 on: Harry Potter, The Lord of the Rings, The Hobbit, A Song of Ice and Fire, Strugatsky brothers, Pelevin, Stephen King, Agatha Christie late works, bestsellers, sci fi and fantasy, author stories.
Fairy tales and children's books: Russian folk tales, Pushkin's tales, Grimm, Andersen, Perrault, Alice, Pinocchio and Buratino, Winnie the Pooh, Carlson; their original darker versions and origins.
